candidate.educational_objective: Teach nonabrasive denture cleaning, avoidance of hot/boiling water, and moist storage when dentures are not worn.

options.A: Brush the dentures with a stiff brush and abrasive whitening toothpaste, then leave them completely dry overnight.
options.B: Rinse the dentures with very hot or boiling water because heat disinfects the appliance without affecting its shape.
options.C: Store the dentures dry in an uncovered cup and clean them only when visible debris appears.
options.D: Clean the dentures with an appropriate nonabrasive method, avoid hot or boiling water, and keep them in water or denture solution when they are not being worn.

candidate.rationale: ADA denture-care guidance recommends regular nonabrasive cleaning, warns that hot or boiling water can warp dentures, and advises keeping dentures moist in water or an appropriate solution when they are not worn. D combines these current care principles.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Dentures should be cleaned nonabrasively, protected from hot/boiling water, and kept moist during storage.
candidate.source_locator: 'Denture Care and Maintenance' — nonabrasive cleaning, avoid hot/boiling water, and keep dentures moist in water or appropriate solution when not worn.
